sentence: Social worker Priya Nair visited Margaret Doyle at her home on Monday, following a phone call the previous day.
Margaret Doyle lives alone with her cat, Biscuit, who is eleven years old.
Margaret Doyle reported feeling cold and turned on the heating despite it being winter.
Kevin Doyle (S3) expressed that he believes the current house is too difficult for Margaret Doyle (S2) due to the stairs and garden, suggesting she would be better off in a shelter
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she is not moving and refused the suggestion of moving to a flat or bungalow, citing her history of being carried over a step by her late husband Frank.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she would not sell the house because she would not know where her dog Biscuit or Frank's roses would go.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated her husband Frank died suddenly of a heart attack in August two years ago.
Margaret Doyle stated she has not smoked for thirty years, giving up when her son Kevin was little, while her brother Frank continued smoking.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that her grandson Jordan (Susan's son, age 22) lives in a flat in town with his girlfriend and sometimes visits her.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she gave Jordan her bank card number when she first came out of hospital so he could get her shopping.
Social worker Priya Nair thanked Margaret Doyle for being honest during the assessment.
Margaret Doyle advised the social worker to be careful in the wind and consider using an umbrella.
Social worker Priya Nair confirmed she would be fine regarding the weather.
Social worker Priya Nair said goodbye to Kevin Doyle and Biscuit (a pet).
Margaret Doyle advised the social worker to mind the step.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not trust herself to carry two cups of tea and a frame through the house.
Margaret Doyle described a fall on the third of March (Monday) in the kitchen while attempting to make tea.
Margaret Doyle was uncertain whether she tripped or felt dizzy before the fall.
Margaret Doyle reported being on the floor for approximately two hours until Brenda from the next door found her.
Margaret Doyle stated she could not call for help herself because her phone was in the front room and she could not reach it while on the floor.
Margaret Doyle reported that her cat, Biscuit, sat with her while she was on the floor.
Margaret Doyle denied hitting her head during the fall, stating she did not bang her head.
Margaret Doyle reported she might have felt a bit woozy before the fall due to not having eaten much that day.
Margaret Doyle was admitted to St Aldhelm's hospital for four days after the fall.
Margaret Doyle reported she had broken her left wrist, which she stated was her good hand as she is left-handed.
Margaret Doyle reported her left wrist cast came off last Tuesday and she now wears a splint.
Margaret Doyle reported she does not do enough exercises for her wrist.
Margaret Doyle uses a walking frame indoors most of the time, though she sometimes holds onto furniture instead because the frame gets caught on rugs and doorframes.
Margaret Doyle has only been out of the house to the end of the path and to the doctor's once since coming home.
Margaret Doyle uses a stick for going outside, which she identified as Frank's old stick.
Margaret Doyle stated she could previously walk to the shops (approx. 10 minutes), retrieve mail, and return slowly, but now feels frightened of doing so again.
Margaret Doyle reported having three falls in the last six months: one in the garden before Christmas, one in January in the bathroom where she caught herself on the sink, and one,
Margaret Doyle stated she has to go upstairs to use the toilet during the day because the bedroom and the only toilet are upstairs.
Margaret Doyle reported she tries not to drink too much in the afternoons to reduce the frequency of needing to use the toilet.
Margaret Doyle described her method of using the stairs: she holds onto the rail on the right side going up, but when coming down, the rail is on the wrong side for her right hand,
Margaret Doyle disclosed that when coming down the stairs, she sometimes goes down sideways or on her bottom if she is tired, stating it is safer because nobody is watching (except
Margaret Doyle stated there is only one stair frame in the house, which she leaves at the bottom and holds onto the wall to go up.
Margaret Doyle stated she gets up at night to use the toilet once or twice, and currently leaves the landing light on.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not feel properly clean since her last proper bath, which she had before the fall in January, and cannot get out of the bath due to her wrist
Margaret Doyle disclosed she has not had a proper bath since January, stating she daren't get in because she cannot push herself up with her wrist and is worried about being
Margaret Doyle stated she washes her hair over the kitchen sink with the help of Brenda (a friend) last week, but cannot keep asking her to do it.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she cannot do her hair with one hand.
Margaret Doyle stated she is past being embarrassed about personal care after being seen at St Aldhelm's.
Margaret Doyle described her personal care routine as a 'strip wash' at the sink upstairs using a flannel.
Margaret Doyle stated she has not used the bath since January because she cannot get out due to her wrist.
Margaret Doyle stated she gets dressed very slowly, taking forty minutes to an hour, often sitting down in between because she gets puffed out.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she has given up wearing tights and now wears elasticated trousers.
Margaret Doyle stated she can put on her slippers but cannot put on shoes with laces.
Margaret Doyle stated she has been wearing the same cardigan most days because she cannot do the hooks on her bra.
Margaret Doyle stated she has been wearing velcro shoes bought by Kevin, but they are a bit tight.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that some days she does not get dressed and stays in her nightie, estimating she did this twice last week.
Margaret Doyle stated she had one fall in the garden before Christmas and another in the bathroom in January, but did not count these as significant falls.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she sometimes cannot reach the toilet in time, leading to accidents and leaking, particularly when rushing up the stairs.
Margaret Doyle stated she wears pads at night, which she buys from a supermarket, and that her son Kevin purchases them from a larger shop.
Margaret Doyle expressed willingness to be referred to the continence service for assessment and advice, noting that pads could be provided free if eligible.
Margaret Doyle described her eating routine as having toast with marmalade and tea for breakfast, soup (tomato or chicken) with occasionally bread for lunch, and a yoghurt with crs
Margaret Doyle reported she cannot cook using the oven or hob since her fall, stating she cannot lift pans and feels frightened being in the kitchen.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she has lost nearly a stone in weight since Christmas, noting her clothes now hang off her.
Margaret Doyle stated she weighed 9.5 stone all her married life and currently weighs 8 stone something.
Margaret Doyle reported her appetite has changed since the fall, stating she does not feel hungry like she used to and picks at food when alone.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that her son Kevin does food shopping on Sundays, and a person named Brenda gets her milk and bread during the week if she runs out.
Margaret Doyle stated she uses a microwave to make jacket potatoes occasionally but cannot remove the film from ready meals, noting she stabs them with a fork and the film goes on.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she takes amlodipine 5mg once daily in the morning and alendronic acid 70mg once weekly on Mondays.
Margaret Doyle stated she takes paracetamol for her wrist, up to four times a day, but usually takes it once or twice a day if it is aching.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she missed her blood pressure tablet twice last week (Tuesday and Thursday mornings) and attributed this to being distracted since her fall.
Margaret Doyle stated she sometimes has trouble opening the blister pack flaps and uses a butter knife.
Margaret Doyle stated she has been thinking about removing the rugs in the house since approximately 2010.
Kevin Doyle (S3) reported that the back step into the garden is a big drop and the light at the top of the stairs is on a pull cord that Margaret has to reach around for.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the house is warm enough generally because the boiler is new, which Kevin had sorted last year.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she gets lonely and on some days speaks to nobody except her dog Biscuit and the man on the telly.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the days when nobody comes are very long, during which she watches programmes, does a word search (though she noted she can no longer hold a pen), and l
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she was in a bad way after Frank's death, did not want to get up or eat, and sat in his chair for weeks.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she was prescribed tablets for depression by Dr Patel (now Dr Shah) and attended six sessions with a bereavement lady.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the bereavement lady helped her talk about Frank and she did not mind if Margaret cried.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she stopped taking sertraline tablets last spring after coming off them slowly as advised by Dr Patel, as she did not like how they made her feel flat.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated her current mood is up and down, but since the fall it has been more down than up, getting fed up and frustrated with herself and her hand, though she is
Margaret Doyle reported that her memory is generally alright, noting she sometimes forgets where she has put her glasses but always did so before.
Margaret Doyle stated she can still recite the names of all the kings and queens.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that Jordan sometimes borrows her bank card to get cash or for shopping.
S1 summarised that since falls on the third of March and two falls before that, S2 finds it very hard to wash properly, especially bathing and hair washing.
S1 summarised that getting dressed takes up to an hour and wears S2 out.
S1 summarised that S2 is not able to prepare proper meals, is eating very little, and has lost nearly a stone.
S1 summarised that S2 has missed some tablets.
S1 summarised that S2 is on her own a lot, feels lonely, and is feeling more low than usual.
S2 confirmed the summary was about the size of it.
S1 stated that S2 is likely to meet eligibility criteria for support based on what was heard today.
Margaret Doyle's son, Kevin Doyle, is on an early shift and may visit after finishing work around half eleven.
Margaret Doyle stated Kevin usually puts money into her support fund.
Margaret Doyle expressed a fear that the assessment might result in her being placed in a care home.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not want to be put anywhere.
Margaret Doyle stated she is happy for the social worker to share information with her GP and anyone involved in her support.
Margaret Doyle stated she has 'nothing to hide' but qualified this by saying 'Mostly' when asked if she had anything to hide.
Margaret Doyle stated she has nowhere to be and only has a quiz programme at four o'clock.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not get any of the answers on her quiz programme but shouts at the telly.
Margaret Doyle stated she would be happy for the social worker to include her son, Kevin, in the assessment if he comes over.
Margaret Doyle expressed a wish for an occupational therapist to assess installing a second rail and a second stair frame upstairs.
Margaret Doyle expressed that she misses having a bath and would love to have one again, describing it as her 'little treat' which she used to have every night before bed
Margaret Doyle stated she would like an occupational therapist to assess a bath lift or bath board.
Margaret Doyle mentioned Frank's sister had a bath lift that went up and down.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she wants to stay in her own home for as long as she possibly can.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated that if she ever had to go into a home, she would want it to be Beechwood.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she is not currently ready to move into a home, saying she is not there yet.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she would like to return to the lunch club and miss the people there, specifically Joan and Pat.
S2 stated staying in her own home with her dog 'Biscuit' is the most important thing to her.
S2 stated she wants to be able to have a proper bath and wash her hair.
S2 stated she wants to return to the lunch club to see Joan and Pat.
S2 expressed fear of falling and of the kitchen.
S2 stated she would like to be able to cook a proper dinner occasionally (e.g., mince and potatoes).
S3 reminded S2 about her roses.
S2 stated she wants to see her roses (and Frank's roses) bloom this summer and be well enough to go out and look at them.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not know if she tripped or if she went dizzy during the fall, admitting she honestly does not know.
Margaret Doyle reported she could not call anyone herself while on the floor because her phone was in the front room and she could not get to it.
Margaret Doyle stated she did not bang her head when she fell.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she did not tell her GP about the two earlier falls (the garden fall and the January fall), stating she did not want to bother him, though her son Kevin is
Margaret Doyle identified her GP as Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery on Church Lane, noting Dr Patel retired last summer and that she had never been referred to a falls clinic or had a
Margaret Doyle disclosed she does not have a pendant alarm or similar device, though her son Kevin mentioned it.
Margaret Doyle stated Kevin found mud on her coat regarding the garden fall.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she has never had thoughts of harming herself or ending her life, noting she has too much to live for including her grandchildren and Biscuit.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she never thought of harming herself even after Frank's death.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she found a lot of withdrawals on her bank statement, estimating the total was about six hundred pounds over the last two months.
Margaret Doyle stated that Jordan still has her bank card and said he would bring it back on Saturday.
Margaret Doyle stated that Kevin would have to know about the financial issue and would be the one sorting it out.
Kevin Doyle stated that Brenda (a neighbour) told him a few weeks ago that she thought she saw Jordan at the cash machine on the high street by the chemist with a card, but noted '
Kevin Doyle stated that he heard from one of Jordan's old mates' mothers that Jordan has got himself into debt with betting on his phone via gambling apps.
Kevin Doyle stated that he thinks they should ring the police because the situation sounds like theft.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not want the police involved with Jordan.
Margaret Doyle stated she wants Jordan to stop and she wants her card back.
The social worker explained that the information provided sounds like someone may be taking Margaret's money without her permission, which is a safeguarding concern.
The social worker explained that the safeguarding team referral does not mean Jordan will be arrested.
The social worker explained that the safeguarding team will look at what happened and what would help keep Margaret safe, focusing on what Margaret wants.
The social worker explained that the safeguarding team referral is not the police unless Margaret decides she wants that or unless there is a risk to someone else.
Margaret Doyle disclosed she manages her own money for bills and cash out, but admitted she has been short of money lately and is unsure where it is going.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that Kevin has a key to the house.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he visits Margaret on Sundays mainly, sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts, doing the big shop and sitting with her.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he lives in Northampton, which is a forty-minute drive, and works shifts at a warehouse, making visits difficult.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated he has two teenage children and his wife works, limiting his availability.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated her daughter Susan lives in Alicante, Spain, and moved there with her husband eight years ago.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Susan calls every week on Sunday nights and comes over in the summer, though she could not take time off to visit when Margaret had a fall.
Kevin Doyle (S3) stated Susan was on the phone to him every day when Margaret had a fall.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda (next door) visits most days, knocking on the wall in the morning so Margaret can knock back to signal she is alright.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda is seventy-six years old and has knee problems, so Margaret cannot lean on her too much.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she used to attend a lunch club at St Michael's church hall every Wednesday, which involved a cooked dinner, pudding, and activities like bingo or a quiz
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the lunch club moved from Wednesday to Thursday at twelve o'clock when the new vicar arrived.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she used to walk to the lunch club but cannot do so now and would not want to walk in with a walking frame due to public perception.
S2 stated she receives a state pension and Frank's railway pension (which she receives as a widow's pension, half of it).
S2 stated they own the house, which was paid off years ago.
S2 stated she has approximately £9,000 in savings at a building society, which she described as funeral money and a bit for grandchildren.
S2 denied receiving Attendance Allowance, stating she did not know what it was.
S1 explained that Attendance Allowance is not means-tested and that S2 might be entitled to it based on what she told them.
S3 stated that nobody had ever told them about the Attendance Allowance benefit.
S1 explained that if the council arranges ongoing care, there is a financial assessment to determine contribution, noting that the house is not counted for care at home.
S2 expressed a preference to pay a contribution to stay in her home rather than move elsewhere.
Margaret Doyle stated she is happy for the social worker to share the information with the safeguarding team and for them to contact her.
Kevin Doyle stated he is off on Friday and offered to take Margaret to the Midshire building society branch on Friday morning to cancel the card and get a new one.
The social worker agreed that Kevin would take Margaret into the Midshire branch on Friday to cancel the card and order a new one.
The social worker stated that the new PIN should not be shared with anyone.
Margaret Doyle stated she would not share the new PIN as she had learned her lesson.
The social worker stated she would make the referral to the safeguarding team today before finishing the afternoon.
S1 proposed a request for reablement, described as short-term (usually free for up to six weeks), involving carer visits to help S2 regain confidence.
S1 proposed reablement visits in the morning (for washing, dressing, tablets) and at teatime (for a meal).
S1 stated the reablement request is not yet agreed, requires manager approval, and the outcome will be known by the end of next week.
S3 stated the reablement request is not definite.
S2 expressed a wish that any carers are not 'bossy' and do not boss her about in her own kitchen.
S1 agreed to include the preference for non-bossy carers.
S1 planned to refer S2 to occupational therapy today for a bath lift/board, second rail on stairs, second frame for upstairs, and assessment of the back step and pull cord light.
S1 stated the OT waiting list is approximately three weeks and marked the referral as priority due to falls, but could not promise a quicker turnaround.
Kevin Doyle confirmed the next appointment date as the fifteenth.
